title: A standalone-launched `cam sidecar` never writes .cam-sidecar.pid, so every CLI gate (plan/next/ship) reports it dead while it runs healthily
description:
MEASURED LIVE, not inferred. After a coherence rebuild this session, `pgrep -fl 'cam sidecar'` showed a healthy single sidecar at pid 77410 (ppid 1), while `cam plan 382` refused with 'sidecar is not running -- run `cam run` to start the sidecar'. The gate was correct about the file and wrong about the world: .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid still contained 65540, a pid from the PREVIOUS session, with an mtime predating the respawn.

ROOT CAUSE, read from source rather than guessed:
- src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts:97 `sidecarAlive(claudeDir)` = readSidecarPid() + signal-0 probe. It trusts the pidfile as the sole source of truth for WHICH pid to probe.
- `writeSidecarPid` has exactly ONE production spawn call site: src/commands/run.ts:815, immediately after `cam run` spawns the sidecar as its own child.
- The standalone `cam sidecar` subcommand does NOT write the pidfile for itself.

CONSEQUENCE: any sidecar started outside `cam run`'s spawn path -- which is precisely what the documented coherence-rebuild procedure does (`nohup cam sidecar > .claude/cam-supervisor.log 2>&1 & disown`, run after every rebuild that touches sidecar-executed code) -- is invisible to src/commands/sidecar-gate.ts. `cam plan`, `cam next` and `cam ship` all refuse to write their phase/active signal, and the refusal text sends the operator to `cam run`, which is the wrong remedy and would spawn a SECOND orchestrator session.

This is not a rare edge: the coherence rebuild runs at the end of most cycles, so the gate is left stale-by-construction on a routine path. It was latent for a full cycle before it bit.

WORKAROUND APPLIED THIS SESSION (record-correction, not a fix): hand-wrote the true live pid into .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid. The pidfile's contract is 'the sidecar's pid'; it simply held a false value.

DIRECTION: have the sidecar persist its OWN pid at startup, inside the `cam sidecar` entry point, so the record is written by the process it describes rather than by one particular parent that happens to spawn it. That makes the pidfile correct under every launch path, including run.ts's, whose existing write then becomes redundant rather than load-bearing. Consider also removing the pidfile on clean sidecar exit.

Secondary, worth deciding separately: sidecar-gate's refusal message hardcodes `cam run` as the remedy. Once the sidecar self-registers this is mostly moot, but a gate that says 'not running' when the process IS running is a bad failure mode regardless; a stale-pidfile-vs-live-process mismatch could be detected and reported distinctly.

Needs rebuild: both the sidecar entry point and sidecar-gate are binary-executed.

spec.scope: The standalone `cam sidecar` process never writes .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid, so the CLI liveness gate (cam plan/next/ship, via sidecarLivenessGate -> sidecarAlive) refuses against a healthy sidecar whenever it was started outside `cam run`'s spawn path -- exactly what the documented coherence-rebuild ritual does (nohup cam sidecar ...). Root-cause fix (locus A): have runSidecar (src/commands/sidecar.ts) self-register its OWN pid at boot by calling writeSidecarPid(claudeDir, process.pid), through a NEW injectable DI seam options.writeSidecarPidFn that defaults to writeSidecarPid, placed adjacent to the existing writeSessionStartFn boot record (before the poll loop) and mirroring that exact seam pattern. Add the import of writeSidecarPid into src/commands/sidecar.ts. This makes the pidfile correct under EVERY launch path (including run.ts's existing write, which becomes redundant-but-harmless since it writes the same pid) and is inherently project-scoped via claudeDir. Add a behavioral regression test proving self-registration. NON-GOALS (explicitly out of scope): removing the pidfile on exit / adding any SIGTERM/SIGINT/exit handler (runSidecar currently has none, teardown is owned by the parent `cam run`, and signal-0 already correctly reports a dead stale pid as not-running); the pgrep/global-process-scan alternative (locus B), which is project-blind because the sidecar argv is just ['cam','sidecar'] with no project marker; and changing sidecar-gate's refusal message. Needs a coherence rebuild after merge (sidecar-executed code).
acceptanceCriteria: runSidecar self-registers the sidecar's own pid at boot: a new test at test/supervisor/sidecar-self-pid.test.ts boots runSidecar with an injected immediately-resolving runSidecarLoopFn and cwd set to a fresh temp dir, then asserts sidecarAlive(join(tmpCwd, '.claude')) is true afterward (the pidfile now holds the live pid). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-self-pid.test.ts]

The self-write goes through a new injectable DI seam named writeSidecarPidFn, consistent with the existing writeSessionStartFn seam. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'writeSidecarPidFn' src/commands/sidecar.ts]
The existing pid-helper suite still passes (no regression to writeSidecarPid/readSidecarPid/sidecarAlive/removeSidecarPid). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-pid.test.ts]

Reviewer confirms: the self-write is placed at boot before the poll loop via the writeSidecarPidFn DI seam (mirroring writeSessionStartFn); writeSidecarPid is imported into sidecar.ts; it writes process.pid into the per-project claudeDir (project-scoped, no global process scan is introduced); run.ts's existing writeSidecarPid call is left untouched and remains correct as a redundant same-pid write; and the NON-GOAL is respected (no new SIGTERM/SIGINT/exit handler, no remove-on-exit, refusal message unchanged). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
gotchas: writeSidecarPid is NOT currently imported in src/commands/sidecar.ts (grep confirms 0 occurrences) -- add the import from the sidecar-pid module (src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts).

Place the self-write adjacent to the writeSessionStartFn call (~src/commands/sidecar.ts:3383), which sits BEFORE the runContainerEnsureGuard early-return -- same boot position as the existing session-start record, so the pidfile is written as early as the other boot records.

Follow the existing DI-seam pattern exactly: add writeSidecarPidFn?: (claudeDir: string, pid: number) => void to SidecarOptions, and call (options.writeSidecarPidFn ?? writeSidecarPid)(claudeDir, process.pid).

The behavioral test must inject options.runSidecarLoopFn to resolve immediately (runSidecar's loop otherwise never resolves). Many existing tests already boot runSidecar (e.g. test/sidecar-ship-phase.test.ts, test/commands/sidecar-plan-phase-orphan-sweep.test.ts) -- mirror their stubbing + the temp-dir style of test/supervisor/sidecar-pid.test.ts (mkdtempSync + rmSync cleanup). Set cwd to the temp dir so claudeDir resolves under it. The test filename MUST be exactly test/supervisor/sidecar-self-pid.test.ts (AC1 oracle references it).

Do NOT touch run.ts's existing writeSidecarPid(join(cwd,'.claude'), sidecarProc.pid) call or its cleanup removeSidecarPidIfExists -- they stay; the self-write just makes the sidecar's own boot the authoritative writer.
Do NOT add remove-on-exit or any signal handler (explicit NON-GOAL); do NOT introduce a pgrep/global process scan (locus B is project-blind).
